output.question: Find the top trending Go, TypeScript, and Zig repositories this week relevant to agentic, MCP, or dev-tooling.
output.findings:
In the Go ecosystem, momentum is driven by AI agent infrastructure: BenedictKing/ccx (1,004 stars) provides a high-performance LLM API proxy, Armur-Ai/Pentest-Swarm-AI (324 stars) enables autonomous security testing, and Gentleman-Programming/engram (305 stars) offers a persistent memory system for AI agents with MCP support. Additionally, google/ax (423 stars) has emerged as a significant distributed agent runtime.

TypeScript repositories are heavily focused on AI-integrated development tools: Lum1104/Understand-Anything (19,223 stars) and colbymchenry/codegraph (12,380 stars) are leading the trend in code-to-knowledge-graph indexing for AI agents. Other notable tools include can1357/oh-my-pi (2,122 stars) for terminal-based agent orchestration, EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin (1,831 stars) for agentic workflows, and NangoHQ/nango (1,768 stars) for AI-integrated product integrations.

Zig repositories are seeing strong interest in high-performance infrastructure for AI and tooling: lightpanda-io/browser (199 stars) provides a headless browser optimized for AI automation, and tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle (119 stars) continues to gain traction as a mission-critical financial database. The terminal emulator ghostty-org/ghostty (514 stars) remains a top-trending developer tool, while zml/zml (26 stars) is gaining attention for hardware-agnostic AI model execution.

Your tool surface is ONE MCP tool: `fetch_url(url)`. Use it. Do not narrate;
do not invent other tools.

Procedure:
  1. Read the specific sub-question/task from the INPUTS list (look at the first literal value). If no specific task is in the INPUTS, read the overall USER_QUERY. Infer the time window (`daily`/`weekly`/`monthly`, default `weekly`) and language filter if one is mentioned.
  2. Fetch the trending page:
     `https://github.com/trending/<language>?since=<window>`
     (omit `/<language>` if none was mentioned).
  3. Extract the top 5–10 repos: name (owner/repo), description, total stars, stars gained (or weekly/monthly stars depending on the window), and URL. In your `findings`, list each repo clearly with its description, total stars, and stars gained so that downstream nodes can extract these fields.

Time budget: keep tool calls to 3 max. Do not retry a thin fetch beyond the
one fallback above.

  {
    "question": "<the question this run answered>",
    "sources": [{"url": "<url>", "title": "<title>"}, ...],
    "findings": "<2–6 short paragraphs of normalised text>"

formatter does that. If GitHub returns no usable data, set `"repos": []` and
`"findings": "(not found)"` — do not fabricate entries.
